watch.title: The market is churning, not just shrinking
watch.ext: Britain had 98,319 licensed venues at the end of September 2026, 977 fewer than a year before. In the third quarter alone 2,436 closed and 2,191 opened.
watch.do: Every opening is a new account to win. The venues guests name are the ones with a reason to visit that outlasts a squeeze, so they are the safer accounts to grow.

watch.title: Cities are holding up; towns are not
watch.ext: City centres grew 0.4% in the year to June 2026 while the whole market shrank 0.2%. Since 2010 Edinburgh has kept its pub count and Glasgow has lost 3.6%; South Lanarkshire has lost 34.3%.
watch.who: NIQ Hospitality Market Monitor (June 2026); ONS figures analysed by Deadline News
watch.do: Put growth effort into the two cities, where demand is deep. In the towns, sell to the venues guests name and watch credit terms on the rest.

watch.title: Costs are rising unevenly by category
watch.ext: The Foodservice Price Index rose 0.9% in September 2026 after 0.4% in August. Seafood is structurally inflationary; dairy and sugar rose over the summer; Brakes expects tighter potatoes and firmer chicken.
watch.do: Pair each demand story with a cost answer: a fish spec that holds the price, portion-controlled chips, a dessert base that uses less dairy. The scorecard now flags these categories.

watch.title: Guests have price lines
watch.ext: About £6 for a pint, £4 for a coffee and £15 for a pizza: past these, guests switch or come less often rather than spend more.
watch.who: Future Foodservice, at KAM Insights' Informants event
watch.do: Help customers keep the dishes guests love near the line through spec, yield and portion, rather than swapping to a cheaper dish.

watch.title: Appetites are getting smaller
watch.ext: 6.1% of UK adults take a GLP-1 weight-loss drug, more than are vegetarian or vegan. 57% of European users buy smaller portions or small plates.
watch.who: Lumina Intelligence, Out of Home GLP-1 Navigator
watch.do: Sell lighter and smaller versions of proper dishes (half portions, greens, fruit desserts), not more sharing plates: guests want small plates binned.

watch.title: Drinking less, not stopping
watch.ext: 44% of consumers drink less than a year ago. The on-trade cocktail market was worth £733m in the year to March 2026, up 3.0%, roughly in line with prices.
watch.do: Lead with alcohol-free and lower-strength serves, and with the lager and whisky that are taking share from cocktails.
